children: A vessel was struck by a projectile while traveling through the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, Reuters reported, adding to concerns that escalating Middle East attacks could further disrupt global energy supplies.
The U.K. Maritime Trade Operations agency said the ship caught fire and its crew was evacuated by local authorities. No group immediately claimed responsibility.

The incident followed Saudi Arabia’s precautionary closure of its East-West oil pipeline after a drone attack said to have been launched from Iraq. The pipeline has become a critical outlet because war has sharply reduced shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. It has recently carried 4 million to 5 million barrels a day, equal to roughly 4% to 5% of global oil consumption.
The attacks threaten both major routes used to move Gulf oil: Hormuz and Saudi Arabia’s alternative pipeline to the Red Sea. A prolonged interruption could tighten global supplies, keep Brent crude

above $100 a barrel and raise fuel and transportation costs. Oil producers and tanker operators may benefit from higher prices and freight rates, while airlines, manufacturers, retailers and other fuel-intensive businesses face pressure on margins. Renewed energy inflation also could complicate the outlook for interest rates.

Regional hostilities are spreading. Saudi Arabia reported additional projectile damage near its border with Yemen, while Iranian media said an Iranian commercial vessel was attacked off the country’s southern coast. Houthi forces also claimed Saudi airstrikes in Yemen and were reported to have captured Perim Island, a strategic position in the Bab el-Mandeb shipping passage.

Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has asked Washington for military assistance against the Houthis. The United States has reportedly offered intelligence support but has so far declined direct intervention.

Iran is expected to meet Gulf Arab states in Oman to discuss Hormuz, though expectations for an agreement remain low, Reuters reported. Tehran is seeking recognition of its authority to collect fees from ships using the waterway, a demand rejected by Washington. Iran has indicated that the strait will not reopen fully unless its broader conditions are met.

title: Hormuz ship attack deepens oil supply fears after Saudi pipeline closure
